narrative_purpose: Makes Fick's law visual: gas crosses a living membrane faster with more surface, a thinner wall, and a steeper difference between the two sides.
subject: A microscopic cross-section of a delicate biological respiratory membrane. On the left side, a dense concentration of luminescent cyan dissolved gas particles in a micro-fluid chamber; in the center, an ultra-thin translucent folded biological tissue membrane barrier maximizing surface area; on the right side, a perfused capillary lumen with sparse glowing teal molecules rapidly whisked away by circulating hemolymph.
scene: High-magnification histological cutaway specimen against deep indigo shadow, highlighting the microscopic architecture of gas diffusion across living tissue.
camera: Direct microscopic cross-section view with clear focal plane on the membrane barrier.
light: Bioluminescent key light radiating from the dense cyan gas particles and subtle interior glow of the capillary bed.
palette: Void indigo background #070912, dense cyan #36c5d9 on left, delicate living teal #2bd4a8 membrane, pale capillary lumen.
style: Painterly naturalist histological specimen illustration, oil texture, luminous biological key light, spec-bio field guide plate.
detail_level: Crisp cellular membrane texture, distinct particle density gradient across the barrier, delicate capillary wall folds.
